lines.differs: Worse for AtliQ than Acme Retail Group: same 0.5% weekly rate capped at 5%, but lacks Acme's explicit exclusions for client-caused delays.
Better for AtliQ than Brightwater Insurance Inc: 0.5% per week capped at 5% of milestone fee, versus 1% of total contract value per day uncapped.
Better for AtliQ than Al Noor Hospitality Group: penalty is 0.5% per week capped at 5% of milestone fee, instead of 1% uncapped.
Same as Orbit Travels Pvt Ltd: deliverables transfer upon payment while pre-existing materials are retained by AtliQ.
Worse for AtliQ than Rohan Iyer: ownership of deliverables transfers to the client upon payment, rather than AtliQ retaining full ownership.
Same as Crestline Retail Inc: deliverables transfer to the client upon payment while AtliQ retains pre-existing materials under a non-exclusive perpetual license.
Worse for AtliQ than Rohan Iyer: liability is capped at the total contract price without excluding indirect or consequential damages.
Worse for AtliQ than PayTrack Technologies: liability is limited to the contract price but lacks an exclusion for indirect and consequential damages.
Worse for AtliQ than Sunrise Foods: liability cap covers total contract price but does not exclude indirect, consequential, or lost profit damages.
Worse for AtliQ than Acme Retail Group: mandates compliance with Bahrain data protection law instead of India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023.
Worse for AtliQ than Sunrise Foods: requires compliance with Bahrain data protection law rather than Indian data protection laws.
Better for AtliQ than Northwind Logistics: requires compliance with Bahrain data law only, avoiding UK GDPR rules, documented instruction limits, and transfer addenda.
Worse for AtliQ than Al Noor Hospitality Group: governs under Bahrain law and BCDR without a mandatory 30-day good-faith executive negotiation period.
Worse for AtliQ than CloudSpan Technologies: subjects disputes to Bahrain law and BCDR directly, lacking a 30-day executive negotiation period prior to proceedings.
Worse for AtliQ than Northwind Logistics: governed by Bahrain law and BCDR rather than English law and neutral LCIA international arbitration in London.
